newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy tyre sales seen down 10 pct in Jan-Oct - study.
newsitem.headline: Italy tyre sales seen down 10 pct in Jan-Oct - study.

text.p: Sales of tyres in Italy in the first 10 months of this year are down 10 percent on the same year-ago period, a sector research body said.
Autopromotec said in a report that Italy was the European country where car owners changed their tyres the least frequently.

The study said that in Italy last year only 60 tyres - new or retreads - per 100 cars on the road were sold. This compared with 92 in France and Britain, 94 in Germany and the highest figure of 141 in Ireland.
Autopromotec said the fall in tyre sales was partly due to a slump in consumer demand in the first half of this year.
But it also said that Italian car owners had the habit of delaying changing their tyres "far too often well beyond the legal safety limits".

It noted that Italian law forbids driving with tyres which have a tread depth of less than 1.6 mm. "But unfortunately the safety requirements too often clash with the need to save money, and it is probably this aspect which is behind the worsening of the sales situation this year."

However, the situation could improve in the medium term due to new government rules on car road tests under which cars must have an official road test every four years instead of every 10 years currently.

In such a case drivers would in theory be forced to change worn out tyres in order to pass the test. Autopromotec noted, however, that current police checks on the state of car tyres were "practically inexistent."
